1	# Boldteq Software Factory — Master Overview
2	
3	This document is the single source of truth for the entire Boldteq Software Factory system. If you have lost everything and are starting from scratch, start here, then follow the numbered docs in order.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## What Is This System?
8	
9	The Boldteq Software Factory is a local AI-powered development infrastructure that runs on your Mac. It turns Claude Code (the VS Code extension) from a general-purpose assistant into a coordinated team of 12 specialist agents that know your stack, your standards, and your active projects.
10	
11	Every component in this system has one job. They are designed to work together without requiring you to repeat context.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## The Five Components
16	
17	### 1. Claude Hub — The Control Center
18	
19	**Location:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/`
20	
21	Claude Hub is a local web application running on `http://localhost:3847`. It has two parts:
22	
23	- **Express backend** (`src/server.js`) — REST API that reads/writes agent files, CLAUDE.md files, slash commands, and handles orchestration runs and playground agent calls.
24	- **React/TypeScript/Vite frontend** (`client/`) — The browser dashboard you use to manage everything.
25	
26	Claude Hub is kept alive 24/7 by pm2 and auto-starts on macOS login via a LaunchAgent. You never manually start it.
27	
28	Pages in the dashboard:
29	- **Dashboard** — overview of all projects, agents, and commands
30	- **All Agents** — browse and edit all 12 global agents
31	- **All Commands** — browse slash commands across all projects
32	- **Orchestration** — visual DAG workflow builder for chaining agents
33	- **Playground** — test any single agent interactively
34	- **Global CLAUDE.md** — view and edit the global instruction file
35	- **Project Detail** — per-project agents, commands, and CLAUDE.md
36	- **Setup & Status** — system health, SDK installer, project directories
37	- **Settings** — project directory configuration
38	
39	### 2. Global CLAUDE.md — The Briefing File
40	
41	**Location:** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
42	
43	Every single Claude Code session in every project reads this file first. It contains the Boldteq identity, build standards, agent routing rules, and active project list. It is the foundation that makes Claude Code behave consistently across all projects. Without it, Claude Code has no knowledge of your stack, agents, or standards.
44	
45	### 3. The Agent Roster — The Specialist Team
46	
47	**Location:** `~/.claude/agents/`
48	
49	12 `.md` files, each one a specialist persona with a name, model, and system prompt. Claude Code loads all of them at startup and can route tasks to the right specialist automatically. You can also invoke them explicitly by name. The agents cover the entire build lifecycle from research to deployment to monitoring.
50	
51	### 4. The SDK — Programmatic Agent Access
52	
53	**Location:** `claude-hub/sdk/` (installed as `@boldteq/agents` in each project)
54	
55	A tiny Node.js package that lets any project call any agent over HTTP with one line of code. It posts to Claude Hub which runs `claude -p` with the agent's instructions and streams back the result. Zero cost beyond the existing Claude subscription.
56	
57	### 5. Slash Commands — Repeatable Workflows
58	
59	**Location:** `[project]/.claude/commands/`
60	
61	`.md` files that become `/commandname` shortcuts in Claude Code chat. Pinzo has `/feature`, `/fix`, `/review`, and `/db`. These are pre-written, detailed instructions for the most common workflows in that project. You type the command, pass arguments, and Claude Code executes the full workflow.
62

1	# Claude Hub — Complete Setup Guide
2	
3	This guide walks you through setting up the entire Claude Hub system from zero. By the end, Claude Hub will be running permanently in the background, auto-starting on every login, and all 12 agents will be available in every Claude Code session.
4	
5	If any step fails, jump to the TROUBLESHOOTING section at the bottom.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Prerequisites
10	
11	### Why each prerequisite matters
12	
13	Before installing anything, verify that the right versions are present. The system has been tested and runs on these specific versions. Older versions may work but are not guaranteed.
14	
15	### Node.js 20+
16	
17	Claude Hub's backend is a Node.js Express server. The `@boldteq/agents` SDK uses the native `fetch` API which requires Node 18+. The current setup uses **Node 20.20.1 via nvm**.
18	
19	```bash
20	node --version
21	```
22	
23	Expected output:
24	```
25	v20.20.1
26	```
27	
28	If not installed or wrong version:
29	
30	```bash
31	# Install nvm (Node Version Manager)
32	curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
33	
34	# Reload shell
35	source ~/.zshrc
36	
37	# Install Node 20
38	nvm install 20
39	nvm use 20
40	nvm alias default 20
41	
42	# Verify
43	node --version
44	# v20.x.x
45	```
46	
47	📝 When you install Node via nvm, the binary lives at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.x.x/bin/node`. This exact path is used in the LaunchAgent plist. If you change Node versions later, you must update the plist.
48	
49	### npm 9+
50	
51	Ships automatically with Node 18+. Verify:
52	
53	```bash
54	npm --version
55	```
56	
57	Expected output:
58	```
59	10.8.2
60	```
61	
62	No manual installation needed if Node is correct.
63	
64	### pm2 (Process Manager)
65	
66	pm2 keeps Claude Hub running permanently even after closing your terminal. It restarts the process if it crashes, and persists the process list across reboots.
67	
68	```bash
69	npm install -g pm2
70	pm2 --version
71	```
72	
73	Expected output:
74	```
75	6.0.14
76	```
77	
78	If not installed:
79	```bash
80	npm install -g pm2
81	```
82	
83	📝 The `-g` flag installs pm2 globally so it's accessible from any directory and as a system command.
84	
85	### Claude Code (CLI)
86	
87	Claude Hub calls the `claude` CLI to run agents. This must be installed and authenticated.
88	
89	```bash
90	claude --version
91	```
92	
93	Expected output (something like):
94	```
95	Claude Code 1.x.x
96	```
97	
98	If not installed, go to https://claude.ai/code and follow the installation instructions. After installing, authenticate:
99	
100	```bash
101	claude login
102	```
103	
104	⚠️ Claude Hub will not be able to run agents (Playground, Orchestration) if `claude` is not authenticated. The dashboard itself will still work.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Step 1 — Verify the Claude Hub Directory
109	
110	Why this matters: Claude Hub must live at a specific absolute path because that path is hardcoded in `ecosystem.config.js` and the LaunchAgent plist. Moving it after setup requires updating those files.
111	
112	```bash
113	ls "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/"
114	```
115	
116	Expected output:
117	```
118	IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKLIST.md
119	ORCHESTRATION_GUIDE.md
120	README.md
121	client/
122	config.json
123	docs/
124	ecosystem.config.js
125	node_modules/
126	orchestrations.json
127	package.json
128	package-lock.json
129	public/
130	public-dist/
131	sdk/
132	src/
133	```
134	
135	Key files to confirm exist:
136	- `src/server.js` — the backend
137	- `ecosystem.config.js` — pm2 configuration
138	- `sdk/` — the @boldteq/agents package
139	- `client/` — the React frontend source
140	- `public-dist/` — the built frontend (served by Express)
141	
142	⚠️ If `public-dist/` is missing or empty, the frontend won't load. See Step 3 for how to build it.
143	
144	### Checking ecosystem.config.js
145	
146	This file tells pm2 how to run Claude Hub. Read it:
147	
148	```bash
149	cat "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/ecosystem.config.js"
150	```
151	
152	Expected content:
153	```javascript
154	module.exports = {
155	  apps: [
156	    {
157	      name: 'claude-hub',
158	      script: './src/server.js',
159	      cwd: '/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub',
160	      interpreter: 'node',
161	      watch: false,
162	      autorestart: true,
163	      max_restarts: 5,
164	      env: {
165	        NODE_ENV: 'production',
166	        PORT: 3847,
167	      },
168	      error_file: '/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-error.log',
169	      out_file: '/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-out.log',
170	      log_date_format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss',
171	    },
172	  ],
173	}
174	```
175	
176	Each field explained:
177	- `name: 'claude-hub'` — the pm2 process name. Used in all pm2 commands.
178	- `script: './src/server.js'` — the entry point, relative to `cwd`.
179	- `cwd: '/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub'` — absolute working directory. If Claude Hub moves, update this.
180	- `watch: false` — do not auto-restart when files change (important for production stability).
181	- `autorestart: true` — restart automatically if the process crashes.

378	## Step 5 — LaunchAgent Setup (Auto-Start on macOS Login)
379	
380	### Why a LaunchAgent?
381	
382	pm2 manages the process, but pm2 itself needs to be started after a reboot. The LaunchAgent is macOS's built-in service system. It runs a specified program when you log in, before you open any apps.
383	
384	Without a LaunchAgent:
385	- After a Mac restart, pm2 is not running
386	- Claude Hub is not running
387	- The SDK fails silently in all projects
388	- You must manually run `pm2 resurrect` or `pm2 start ecosystem.config.js` after every reboot
389	
390	With the LaunchAgent:
391	- Mac restarts → login → LaunchAgent fires → `node src/server.js` starts → Claude Hub is running → all SDK calls work
392	
393	📝 Note: The LaunchAgent in this setup runs Claude Hub **directly** (not via pm2). This is intentional — it guarantees Claude Hub starts even if pm2's process list was lost.

730	# If it returns a PID, kill it

732	
733	# Now start Claude Hub
734	pm2 restart claude-hub
735	# or
736	npm start
737	```

740	```bash

742	# If claude-hub shows online, you're trying to start a second instance. Don't.
743	# If you want to restart it:
744	pm2 restart claude-hub
745	```

1	# Claude Code Agents — Complete Reference
2	
3	This document covers everything about the 12 global agents: what they are, how Claude Code discovers them, how to invoke them, how to create new ones, and how to maintain them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## What Are Agents?
8	
9	An agent is a `.md` file with YAML frontmatter that defines a specialist persona for Claude Code. When Claude Code runs an agent, it reads the file's frontmatter for metadata and uses the file body as the system prompt for that Claude call.
10	
11	Agents solve a specific problem: instead of explaining your entire stack and standards to Claude on every task, you write that context once in the agent file. From then on, invoking `koda` means "use this pre-loaded context about our Shopify stack and feature-building standards."
12	
13	They also allow automatic routing — Claude Code reads all agent `description` fields and can route a task to the right specialist without you explicitly naming one.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## How Claude Code Discovers Agents
18	
19	Claude Code reads all `.md` files in these directories at startup:
20	
21	1. `~/.claude/agents/` — global agents, available in every project
22	2. `[project]/.claude/agents/` — project-level agents, available only in that project
23	
24	No registration or configuration needed. Drop a `.md` file into either directory and it is immediately available in the next Claude Code session.
25	
26	📝 Claude Code loads agents at session start, not on every message. If you create or edit an agent file, open a new chat window to pick up the changes.
27	
28	### File Naming
29	
30	The filename (without `.md`) becomes the agent's slug — the name you use to call it programmatically:
31	- `koda.md` → invoked as `koda`
32	- `nova.md` → invoked as `nova`
33	- `custom-specialist.md` → invoked as `custom-specialist`
34	
35	Names must match the regex `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`. No spaces, no special characters.
36	
37	### Global vs Project-Level Agents
38	
39	| Scope | Directory | Available in |
40	|-------|-----------|-------------|
41	| Global | `~/.claude/agents/` | Every Claude Code session, every project |
42	| Project | `[project]/.claude/agents/` | Only when that project is open |
43	
44	Project-level agents override global agents with the same filename. If `~/.claude/agents/koda.md` and `Pinzo/.claude/agents/koda.md` both exist, Pinzo's version takes priority when working in Pinzo. This lets you specialize a global agent for one project without affecting others.
45	
46	**When to use project-level agents:**
47	- A workflow is too specific to one project to belong globally (e.g., a Pinzo widget specialist)
48	- You want to override a global agent with project-specific context
49	- A project has a unique tech stack that doesn't apply anywhere else
50	
51	**When to keep it global:**
52	- The agent's skills apply to all projects (most agents should be global)
53	- You want Rex to be able to route to this agent from any project
54

57	## The 12 Global Agents
58	
59	These agents cover the entire build lifecycle. They are the "team" that executes work while you make decisions.

61	### Rex — Commander
62	
63	| Field | Value |
64	|-------|-------|
65	| File | `~/.claude/agents/rex.md` |
66	| Model | opus |
67	| Purpose | Master orchestrator. Entry point for any new project or sprint. |
68	
69	Rex owns outcomes, not tasks. Give Rex a brief (one line or ten) and it coordinates the full agent team in the correct order. It does not write code, research, or design — it sequences, delegates, and enforces quality gates.
70	
71	Rex operates in four modes:
72	- **Mode A (New Product Build):** Nova → Arya → Riko → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira
73	- **Mode B (Feature Addition):** Arya → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira
74	- **Mode C (Maintenance/Fix):** Vex → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt
75	- **Mode D (Launch/Go-Live):** Sage → Quill → Bolt → Hawk
76	
77	**Typical inputs:** Product brief, feature request, "fix sprint for Pinzo", "prepare Rankora for launch"
78	**Typical outputs:** Coordinated execution plan, dispatches to specialist agents in order
79	**When NOT to use:** When you already know which specialist you need. Don't route to Rex if you just want Koda to build one component.

87	| File | `~/.claude/agents/nova.md` |
88	| Model | sonnet |
89	| Purpose | Competitive intelligence before building anything new. |

137	| Purpose | All production code — frontend, backend, database, integrations. |

334	## How to Create a New Agent
335	
336	### When to create a new global agent
337	
338	- You have a recurring specialist role that cuts across multiple projects (e.g., a data migration specialist, a Stripe billing expert)
339	- The specialist's context is too long to re-explain in every prompt
340	- You want Claude Code to auto-route to this specialist
341	
342	### When to create a project-level agent instead
343	
344	- The specialist is deeply tied to one project (e.g., Pinzo's widget specialist who knows the exact storefront widget API)
345	- The agent uses project-specific file paths, model names, or business logic
346	- You want to override a global agent's behavior for one project
347	
348	### The agent file format
349	
350	```markdown
351	---
352	name: Agent Display Name
353	description: What this agent does. Be specific — Claude Code uses this to auto-route tasks.
354	model: sonnet
355	tools: Read,Write,Edit,Bash,Glob,Grep
356	---
357	
358	Your agent's system prompt goes here.
359	
360	## Identity
361	Who this agent is. Give it a name and a role.
362	"You are [Name], the [role] for the Boldteq Software Factory."
363	
364	## Responsibilities
365	Exactly what this agent does. Be explicit.
366	- Does X
367	- Does Y
368	- Does NOT do Z (important — define scope boundaries)
369	
370	## Standards
371	What quality standards apply to this agent's output.
372	
373	## Patterns to Use
374	Concrete patterns this agent should always apply.
375	
376	## Patterns to Avoid
377	Antipatterns this agent should never repeat.
378	
379	## Output Format
380	How this agent should structure its responses.
381	```
382	
383	### Frontmatter fields
384	
385	| Field | Required | Values | Notes |
386	|-------|----------|--------|-------|
387	| `name` | Yes | Any string | Shown in Claude Hub UI |
388	| `description` | Yes | Any string | Used for auto-routing — be precise |
389	| `model` | Yes | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku` | Affects cost and quality |
390	| `tools` | No | Comma-separated tool names | Restricts available tools |
391	
392	### Model selection guide
393	
394	| Model | Speed | Cost | Use for |
395	|-------|-------|------|---------|
396	| `haiku` | Fastest | Lowest | Simple tasks: formatting, classification, simple transforms |
397	| `sonnet` | Fast | Medium | Most agents — code generation, research, content writing |
398	| `opus` | Slowest | Highest | Complex reasoning — architecture decisions, orchestration, deep code review |
399	
400	Use `opus` only for Rex, Arya, and Sage. Everything else uses `sonnet`. The cost difference is significant when running many agent calls.
401	
402	### How to write a good description (for auto-routing)
403	
404	The `description` field is what Claude Code reads to decide which agent handles a task. Bad descriptions lead to wrong routing.
405	
406	**Bad description:**
407	```
408	description: Helps with code and stuff
409	```
410	
411	**Good description:**
412	```
413	description: Shopify app bug fixer. Diagnoses and fixes errors in Remix/React Router apps: TypeScript errors, Prisma DB issues, Shopify auth failures, webhook bugs, billing errors. Has category-based diagnostic playbook.
414	```
415	
416	The good description includes: what it does, in what context, what kinds of tasks, and any notable specializations.
417

439	Expected output:

485	## Agent Quality Tips
486	
487	### What makes agent instructions good
488	
489	1. **Clear identity** — the agent knows exactly who it is and what its scope is
490	2. **Explicit non-responsibilities** — saying "you do NOT write tests" is as important as saying what it does do
491	3. **Concrete patterns** — "use `upsert` for singleton records" beats "handle data correctly"
492	4. **Output format specified** — the agent knows what shape to return results in
493	5. **Quality gates explicit** — the agent knows what "done" means
494	
495	### What makes agent instructions bad
496	
497	1. **Too broad** — "help with any code task" gives no routing signal
498	2. **Missing context** — agent doesn't know the stack, framework versions, or project structure
499	3. **No scope boundary** — agent will attempt everything instead of knowing when to hand off
500	4. **Ambiguous instructions** — "handle errors properly" vs "wrap every action in try/catch and return `{ error: msg }` with status 500"
501	5. **No output format** — agent returns different structures on every call
502	
503	### The "one clear responsibility" rule
504	
505	Each agent should be able to answer "what is the one thing you are the expert on?" in one sentence. If the answer requires "and also...", split into multiple agents or make the description more specific.
506	
507	Koda builds features. Vex fixes bugs. Luna tests. Sage reviews. They do not step on each other's territory because their scope boundaries are explicit in their files.
508

1	# @boldteq/agents SDK — Complete Reference
2	
3	This document covers the `@boldteq/agents` SDK: what it is, how it works internally, how to install it in a new project, and the full API reference with examples.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## What the SDK Is and the Problem It Solves
8	
9	Every Boldteq project occasionally needs to call a Claude agent programmatically — not just interactively from a chat window. Examples:
10	
11	- An API route in Rankora that calls Quill to generate a job description summary
12	- A Pinzo webhook handler that calls Vex to diagnose an error and log the diagnosis
13	- A build script that calls Nova to research a competitor before a planning session
14	- An admin dashboard action that calls Koda to auto-generate code suggestions
15	
16	Without the SDK, doing this requires: knowing the `claude` CLI syntax, managing subprocesses, parsing SSE output, handling timeouts, and writing error handling from scratch — every time, in every project.
17	
18	The SDK wraps all of that into a single function:
19	
20	```javascript
21	const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write App Store listing for Pinzo')
22	```
23	
24	That's it. One line. The SDK handles the HTTP call to Claude Hub, which handles the `claude -p` subprocess, SSE streaming, and response parsing. The result comes back as a structured object.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Architecture: How a Call Actually Works
29	
30	```
31	Your code calls:
32	callAgent('quill', 'Write listing for Pinzo')
33	  │
34	  ▼
35	SDK (sdk/index.js)
36	  POST http://localhost:3847/api/playground/run
37	  Body: { agentName: 'quill', prompt: 'Write listing...' }
38	  │
39	  ▼
40	Claude Hub backend (src/server.js)
41	  1. Reads ~/.claude/agents/quill.md
42	  2. Extracts the agent's system prompt (body after frontmatter)
43	  3. Constructs: claude -p "[system prompt]\n\n[user prompt]"
44	  4. Spawns the subprocess
45	  5. Streams output back as Server-Sent Events (SSE)
46	  │
47	  ▼
48	SDK parses the SSE stream:
49	  - Looks for { type: 'done', output: '...' }
50	  - Or { type: 'error', error: '...' }
51	  │
52	  ▼
53	Returns to your code:
54	  { success: true, output: '...the agent response...', agent: 'quill' }
55	  or
56	  { success: false, output: '', agent: 'quill', error: 'reason' }
57	```
58	
59	Key characteristics:
60	- **Zero additional cost** — uses your existing Claude subscription. The `claude -p` subprocess runs under the same authenticated account as your interactive Claude Code sessions.
61	- **Synchronous from your code's perspective** — `await callAgent(...)` blocks until the agent completes or times out.
62	- **Never throws** — the SDK catches all errors internally and returns them in the `error` field. Your code never needs a try/catch around `callAgent`.
63	- **Requires Claude Hub running** — if `http://localhost:3847` is not reachable, the call fails immediately with a "not reachable" error message.

207	```javascript
208	/**
209	 * @boldteq/agents
210	 * Call any global Claude agent from any Boldteq app.
211	 * Claude Hub must be running (auto-starts on login via LaunchAgent).
212	 */
213	
214	const CLAUDE_HUB_URL = process.env.CLAUDE_HUB_URL || 'http://localhost:3847'
215	
216	/**
217	 * Call a global agent with a prompt.
218	 * @param {string} agentName - e.g. "quill", "vex", "nova", "sage", "koda"
219	 * @param {string} prompt - the task to send
220	 * @param {number} [timeoutMs=120000] - timeout in ms
221	 * @returns {Promise<{ success: boolean, output: string, agent: string, error?: string }>}
222	 */
223	async function callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs = 120000) {
224	  const controller = new AbortController()
225	  const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs)
226	
227	  try {
228	    const response = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/playground/run`, {
229	      method: 'POST',
230	      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
231	      body: JSON.stringify({ agentName, prompt }),
232	      signal: controller.signal,
233	    })
234	
235	    clearTimeout(timeout)
236	
237	    if (!response.ok) {
238	      throw new Error(`Claude Hub returned ${response.status}`)
239	    }
240	
241	    const text = await response.text()
242	    const events = text
243	      .split('\n')
244	      .filter(line => line.startsWith('data: '))
245	      .map(line => { try { return JSON.parse(line.slice(6)) } catch { return null } })
246	      .filter(Boolean)
247	
248	    const errorEvent = events.find(e => e.type === 'error')
249	    if (errorEvent) return { success: false, output: '', agent: agentName, error: errorEvent.error }
250	
251	    const doneEvent = events.find(e => e.type === 'done' || e.type === 'complete')
252	    return { success: true, output: doneEvent?.output || '', agent: agentName }
253	
254	  } catch (err) {
255	    clearTimeout(timeout)
256	    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
257	    return {
258	      success: false,
259	      output: '',
260	      agent: agentName,
261	      error: msg.includes('abort')
262	        ? `Timed out after ${timeoutMs / 1000}s`
263	        : `Claude Hub not reachable at ${CLAUDE_HUB_URL} — is it running?`,
264	    }
265	  }
266	}

268	/**

270	 * @returns {Promise<Array<{ filename, name, description, model, body }>>}
271	 */

273	  try {
274	    const res = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/global/agents`)
275	    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)
276	    return await res.json()
277	  } catch {
278	    return []
279	  }
280	}
281	
282	/**
283	 * Check if Claude Hub is reachable.
284	 * @returns {Promise<boolean>}
285	 */
286	async function isOnline() {
287	  try {
288	    const res = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/global/agents`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) })
289	    return res.ok
290	  } catch {
291	    return false
292	  }
293	}

339	## Full API Reference
340	
341	### `callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs?)`
342	
343	The primary function. Calls any global agent with a task and waits for the response.
344	
345	**Parameters:**
346	
347	| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
348	|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
349	| `agentName` | `string` | Yes | — | Agent filename without `.md`. Must match a file in `~/.claude/agents/`. Example: `'koda'`, `'quill'`, `'nova'` |
350	| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | — | The task or instruction to send to the agent. Write it as you would write a message to that specialist. |
351	| `timeoutMs` | `number` | No | `120000` | Maximum time to wait in milliseconds. Default is 2 minutes. Increase for complex tasks. |
352	
353	**Returns:** `Promise<AgentResult>`
354	
355	```typescript
356	interface AgentResult {
357	  success: boolean   // true if the agent ran and returned output
358	  output: string     // the agent's full response text (empty string if success is false)
359	  agent: string      // the agentName that was called (echoed back)
360	  error?: string     // error message (only set if success is false)
361	}
362	```
363	
364	**Examples:**
365	
366	```javascript
367	// Basic call
368	const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write a tagline for Pinzo')
369	if (result.success) {
370	  console.log(result.output)
371	} else {
372	  console.error(result.error)
373	}
374	
375	// With custom timeout for a long task
376	const result = await callAgent(
377	  'koda',
378	  'Build the complete subscription billing page with plan comparison',
379	  300000  // 5 minutes
380	)
381	
382	// Fire and forget (don't await the result)
383	callAgent('mira', 'Extract lessons from today\'s Pinzo session')
384	```
385	
386	**Error scenarios:**
387	
388	The `success: false` result happens when:
389	1. Claude Hub is not reachable: `error` will be "Claude Hub not reachable at http://localhost:3847 — is it running?"
390	2. The call times out: `error` will be "Timed out after Xs"
391	3. Claude Hub returns a non-200 HTTP status
392	4. The `claude` CLI subprocess fails or returns an error event
393

396	### `listAgents()`
397	
398	Fetches all available global agents from Claude Hub.
399	
400	**Returns:** `Promise<Agent[]>`
401	
402	```typescript
403	interface Agent {
404	  filename: string    // filename without .md, e.g. 'koda'
405	  name: string        // display name from frontmatter, e.g. 'Koda — Feature Builder'
406	  description: string // description from frontmatter
407	  model: string       // 'sonnet', 'opus', or 'haiku'
408	  body: string        // full body text (the system prompt)
409	}
410	```
411	
412	Returns an empty array `[]` if Claude Hub is not reachable (does not throw).
413	
414	**Example:**
415	
416	```javascript
417	const agents = await listAgents()
418	agents.forEach(agent => {
419	  console.log(`${agent.filename} (${agent.model}): ${agent.description.slice(0, 60)}...`)
420	})
421	
422	// Output:
423	// arya (opus): Stack selection, data model design, sprint planning...
424	// bolt (sonnet): Deployment to Vercel, Railway, Supabase hardening...
425	// koda (sonnet): All production code — frontend, backend, database...
426	// ...
427	```

429	Use this to dynamically show available agents in a UI, validate an agent name before calling it, or build a picker component.

433	### `isOnline()`
434	
435	Checks if Claude Hub is reachable. Uses a 3-second timeout to avoid blocking.
436	
437	**Returns:** `Promise<boolean>`
438	
439	`true` if Claude Hub responds to `GET /api/global/agents` with a 200 status.
440	`false` if the request fails, times out, or returns a non-200 status.
441	
442	**Example:**
443	
444	```javascript
445	import { isOnline, callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
446	
447	async function generateCopy(product: string) {
448	  if (!await isOnline()) {
449	    throw new Error('Claude Hub is offline. Start it with: pm2 start claude-hub')
450	  }
451	  return await callAgent('quill', `Write a tagline for ${product}`)
452	}
453	```
454	
455	Use `isOnline()` as a guard when Claude Hub being offline would cause a bad user experience (e.g., a UI action that depends on agent output). For fire-and-forget calls (logging, async enrichment), just call the agent directly and handle the error in the result.

546	## Error Handling Patterns
547	
548	### Pattern 1 — Simple check and log
549	
550	```javascript
551	const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write tagline')
552	if (!result.success) {
553	  console.error(`Agent failed: ${result.error}`)
554	  return null
555	}
556	return result.output

559	### Pattern 2 — Distinguish error types
560	
561	```javascript
562	const result = await callAgent('koda', 'Build feature', 300000)
563	
564	if (!result.success) {
565	  if (result.error?.includes('not reachable')) {
566	    // Claude Hub is down
567	    throw new Error('Claude Hub is offline. Run: pm2 start claude-hub')
568	  } else if (result.error?.includes('Timed out')) {
569	    // Task too complex for timeout — retry with longer timeout or smaller task
570	    const retry = await callAgent('koda', 'Build feature (simplified version)', 600000)
571	    return retry.success ? retry.output : null
572	  } else {
573	    // Agent ran but returned an error
574	    console.error('Agent error:', result.error)
575	    return null
576	  }
577	}
578	
579	return result.output
580	```

# Claude Hub — Complete Reference

Claude Hub is a local web application that manages the Boldteq Software Factory: agents, CLAUDE.md files, slash commands, rules, memory, orchestration, and AI tooling — all through a browser dashboard and REST API.

**Architecture:** Express server on `http://localhost:3847`. Serves a React SPA (`public-dist/`) and a REST API. Agent calls stream via SSE. Kept alive by pm2 + macOS LaunchAgent.

---

## The Five Systems

| System | What it is | Global location | Project location |
|--------|-----------|-----------------|------------------|
| CLAUDE.md | Global briefing — read by Claude Code on every session start | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | `[project]/CLAUDE.md` |
| Agents | Specialist `.md` files — define AI personas with system prompts | `~/.claude/agents/` | `[project]/.claude/agents/` |
| Commands | Slash command `.md` files — become `/commandname` shortcuts | N/A | `[project]/.claude/commands/` |
| Rules | Rule `.md` files — project-specific behavioral constraints | N/A | `[project]/.claude/rules/` |
| Memory | Accumulated lessons from all builds | `~/.claude/memory/` | N/A |

---

|------|-------|--------------|
| Dashboard | `/` | Overview of all projects, agents, and system status |
| All Agents | `/agents` | Browse and edit all global agents |

# Setup Guide

Everything needed to get Claude Hub running permanently on a Mac, from zero to fully operational.

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Required version | Check | Install |
|------|-----------------|-------|---------|
| Node.js | 20+ | `node --version` | `nvm install 20 && nvm use 20 && nvm alias default 20` |
| npm | 9+ | `npm --version` | Ships with Node |
| pm2 | Any | `pm2 --version` | `npm install -g pm2` |
| Claude Code CLI | Any | `claude --version` | https://claude.ai/code, then `claude login` |

Node is installed via nvm. The binary lives at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin/node`. This exact path is used in the LaunchAgent plist — if you change Node versions, update it there too.

---

## First-Time Setup (Full Sequence)

### 1. Install dependencies

```bash
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub"
npm install
```

### 2. Start with pm2

```bash
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub"
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js
pm2 save
```

### 3. Verify it's running

```bash
pm2 status
# claude-hub row should show status: online

curl -s http://localhost:3847/api/setup/status
# Returns JSON with system health
```

### 4. Set up LaunchAgent (auto-start on login)

```bash
# Validate the plist exists
ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist

# Load it
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist

# Verify
launchctl list | grep claude-hub
# Expect: a line with a PID number in the first column
```

### 5. Add project directories

- Open http://localhost:3847
- Click Settings
- Add `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App`
- Click Save

### 6. Verify full system

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3847/api/global/agents | python3 -c "import sys,json; a=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(a), 'agents')"
# Expect: 12 agents
```

---

## ecosystem.config.js

Located at `claude-hub/ecosystem.config.js`. Tells pm2 how to run Claude Hub.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  apps: [{
    name: 'claude-hub',
    script: './src/server.js',
    cwd: '/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub',
    interpreter: 'node',
    watch: false,
    autorestart: true,
    max_restarts: 5,
    env: {
      NODE_ENV: 'production',
      PORT: 3847,
    },
    error_file: '/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-error.log',
    out_file: '/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-out.log',
  }]
}
```

Key fields:
- `name: 'claude-hub'` — used in all `pm2` commands
- `cwd` — must be absolute path to claude-hub directory
- `PORT: 3847` — all API calls and browser access use this port
- `autorestart: true` — restarts on crash
- `max_restarts: 5` — stops restarting after 5 consecutive failures

---

## LaunchAgent Plist

Located at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist`. Starts Claude Hub at macOS login, independent of pm2.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>io.boldteq.claude-hub</string>

  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/Users/yashbaldha/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin/node</string>
    <string>/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/src/server.js</string>
  </array>

  <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
  <string>/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub</string>

  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <true/>

  <key>KeepAlive</key>
  <true/>

  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  <string>/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-launchd.log</string>

  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  <string>/Users/yashbaldha/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-launchd-error.log</string>

  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>PORT</key>
    <string>3847</string>
    <key>PATH</key>
    <string>/Users/yashbaldha/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin</string>
  </dict>
</dict>
</plist>
```

To reload after editing:
```bash
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
```

To create from scratch if missing:
```bash
which node   # get your exact node binary path
mkdir -p ~/Library/LaunchAgents
# Then write the plist above, replacing paths with your username
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
```

---

## config.json

Located at `claude-hub/config.json`. Stores project directories.

```json
{
  "projectDirs": [
    "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App"
  ]
}
```

- Tilde `~` in paths is expanded by the server automatically.
- Edit via Settings page or directly — server reads it on each request.
- Claude Hub scans each dir for subdirectories with `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `package.json`, or `pubspec.yaml`.

---

## Settings Page

Access at http://localhost:3847/settings or `/api/global/settings`.

| Setting | What it controls |
|---------|-----------------|
| Project directories | Which folders Claude Hub scans for projects |
| Claude model | Model used by the AI Assistant chat |
| Effort level | Token budget hint for AI responses |
| Permissions JSON | Tool permissions passed to claude CLI |

---

## pm2 Command Reference

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `pm2 status` | Show all processes and their status |
| `pm2 restart claude-hub` | Restart after editing `src/server.js` |
| `pm2 stop claude-hub` | Stop the process (stays in list) |
| `pm2 start claude-hub` | Start a stopped process |
| `pm2 delete claude-hub` | Remove from pm2 entirely |
| `pm2 logs claude-hub` | Stream live logs |
| `pm2 logs claude-hub --lines 50` | Show last 50 log lines |
| `pm2 logs claude-hub --err` | Show error log only |
| `pm2 flush claude-hub` | Clear log files |
| `pm2 save` | Persist process list across reboots |
| `pm2 resurrect` | Restore saved process list after reboot |
| `pm2 monit` | Interactive CPU/memory/log monitor |

---

## Fresh Machine Full Sequence

```bash
# 1. Install Node via nvm
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
source ~/.zshrc
nvm install 20 && nvm use 20 && nvm alias default 20

# 2. Install pm2
npm install -g pm2

# 3. Install Claude CLI and authenticate
# Download from https://claude.ai/code
claude login

# 4. Install Claude Hub deps
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub"
npm install

# 5. Build frontend (if public-dist/ is missing)
npm run build

# 6. Start with pm2
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js
pm2 save

# 7. Load LaunchAgent
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist

# 8. Verify
curl -s http://localhost:3847/api/setup/status
```

---

## Troubleshooting

### EADDRINUSE — port 3847 already in use

```bash
lsof -ti:3847              # find the PID
kill -9 $(lsof -ti:3847)   # kill it
pm2 restart claude-hub
```

If pm2 is already running Claude Hub, don't start another instance — just `pm2 restart claude-hub`.

### pm2 status shows "errored"

```bash
pm2 logs claude-hub --lines 30 --err
```

- `EADDRINUSE` — port conflict, see above.
- `Cannot find module` — run `npm install` in the claude-hub directory.
- `SyntaxError` at a line number — a recent edit broke `server.js`. Test it directly: `node src/server.js`.
- `node: command not found` — pm2 can't find Node. Use the full path in ecosystem.config.js or set `interpreter` to the output of `which node`.

### LaunchAgent not starting (PID shows as `-`)

```bash
# Validate plist syntax
plutil ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
# expect: OK

# Check the error log
cat ~/.pm2/logs/claude-hub-launchd-error.log

# Verify the node binary path in the plist exists
ls /Users/yashbaldha/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin/node

# Fix ownership if wrong
ls -l ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
chown $(whoami):staff ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
```

Reload after fixing:
```bash
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
launchctl list | grep claude-hub
```

### Port conflict between pm2 and LaunchAgent

Both try to bind port 3847 and one will fail. Pick one runner:

```bash
# Option A: LaunchAgent as primary (recommended)
pm2 stop claude-hub && pm2 delete claude-hub

# Option B: pm2 as primary
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
```

### Frontend blank page or "Cannot GET /"

`public-dist/` is missing or empty. Build it:

```bash
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub"
npm run build
pm2 restart claude-hub
```

### After Mac restart, Claude Hub not running

```bash
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist
launchctl list | grep claude-hub
```

If the LaunchAgent keeps failing on restart, fall back to pm2:
```bash
pm2 resurrect
pm2 status
```

Then debug the LaunchAgent separately using the steps above.

### MODULE_NOT_FOUND on startup

```bash
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub"
npm install
pm2 restart claude-hub
```

# Agents

Agents are `.md` files with YAML frontmatter that define specialist AI personas. Claude Code reads them at session start and can route tasks to the right specialist automatically. Each agent is a focused system prompt with a name, model, and defined scope.

---

## Agent File Format

```markdown
---
name: Koda — Feature Builder
description: Writes all production code for any feature. Reads CLAUDE.md and memory first, matches existing patterns, builds types → DB → API → UI in order. Covers Next.js/Supabase (Stack A) and React Router 7/Polaris/Prisma (Stack B).
model: sonnet
tools: Read,Write,Edit,Bash,Glob,Grep
---

## Identity
You are Koda, the Feature Builder for the Boldteq Software Factory.

## Responsibilities
- Build complete, production-grade features from spec
- Read project CLAUDE.md before writing any code
- Follow the build order: types → database → API → UI → integration
- Never use `any` in TypeScript
- Never expose raw errors to the client

## What You Do NOT Do
- Write tests (that's Luna)
- Review code (that's Sage)
- Debug existing bugs (that's Vex)
```

### Frontmatter fields

| Field | Required | Values | Notes |
|-------|----------|--------|-------|
| `name` | Yes | Any string | Shown in Claude Hub UI |
| `description` | Yes | Any string | Used for auto-routing — be specific |
| `model` | Yes | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku` | Affects cost and capability |
| `tools` | No | Comma-separated tool names | Restricts available tools |

### Model selection

| Model | Use for |
|-------|---------|
| `opus` | Rex, Arya, Sage — complex reasoning, orchestration, deep review |
| `sonnet` | All other agents — code, research, content, most tasks |
| `haiku` | Simple classification or formatting only |

---

## Where Agents Live

| Scope | Directory | Available in |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| Global | `~/.claude/agents/` | Every Claude Code session, every project |
| Project | `[project]/.claude/agents/` | Only when that project folder is open |

- Project agents override global agents with the same filename.

| Bolt | `bolt.md` | sonnet | Deploying to production | Vercel/Railway deploy, DB migrations, Shopify App Store submission |
| Quill | `quill.md` | sonnet | App copy, listings, emails | App Store listings, landing pages, Product Hunt, onboarding emails |
| Hawk | `hawk.md` | sonnet | Post-launch monitoring | Sentry setup, uptime, Core Web Vitals, AI cost tracking, incident response |
| Mira | `mira.md` | sonnet | After significant work — training | Extracts lessons from sessions and writes them to `~/.claude/memory/` |

| Task | Agent |
|------|-------|
| New product brief or sprint | Rex |
| Research competitors | Nova |
| Architect a new feature or product | Arya |
| Scaffold a new project | Riko |

| Fix a bug, error, or crash | Vex |

| Pre-deploy review | Sage |
| Deploy to production | Bolt (after Sage approves) |
| Write copy, listings, emails | Quill |
| Set up or respond to monitoring | Hawk |
| Extract lessons from a session | Mira |

**Key rule:** Never deploy without Sage sign-off. Never build features without reading project CLAUDE.md first.

---

## How to Invoke Agents

### In Claude Code chat

```

@nova Research the top 5 Shopify ZIP code delivery apps
@sage Pre-deploy audit of Pinzo — focus on auth and data isolation

const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write an App Store listing for Pinzo')
if (result.success) console.log(result.output)
```

### Via Playground (interactive testing)

1. Open http://localhost:3847/playground
2. Select an agent from the dropdown
3. Type a prompt
4. Click Run — output streams live via SSE

The Playground is the fastest way to test a new agent before integrating it.

## Creating Agents

1. Open http://localhost:3847/agents
2. Click "New Agent"
3. Fill in name, description, model, and body
4. Click Save — file is written to `~/.claude/agents/`

## Copy or Move Agents

Use these endpoints to copy or move agents between global and a project:

## Writing Good Agent Descriptions (Auto-Routing)

The `description` field is what Claude Code reads to route tasks. Vague descriptions cause missed or wrong routing.

**Bad:**
```

```

**Good:**
```

```

Include: what it does, what stack/context, what kinds of tasks, notable specializations.

# @boldteq/agents SDK

The SDK is a small npm package that lets any Boldteq project call any Claude agent programmatically — from a loader, action, API route, or script. One function. No subprocess management. No SSE parsing.

---

## Architecture

```
Your app code
  → callAgent('quill', 'Write listing for Pinzo')
    → POST http://localhost:3847/api/playground/run
      → Claude Hub reads ~/.claude/agents/quill.md
        → Spawns: claude -p "[system prompt]\n\n[user prompt]"
          → Streams SSE output back
            → SDK parses SSE, returns structured result
```

- **Zero extra cost** — uses your existing Claude subscription.
- **Never throws** — all errors are returned in `result.error`, never thrown.
- **Requires Claude Hub running** — if `localhost:3847` is unreachable, the call fails immediately with a clear error message.
- **Server-side only** — never import in browser code. Use in loaders, actions, API routes, and scripts only.

---

## SDK Files

Located at `claude-hub/sdk/`:

| File | What it contains |
|------|-----------------|
| `sdk/package.json` | Package name `@boldteq/agents`, entry point, TypeScript types reference |
| `sdk/index.js` | Runtime — `callAgent`, `listAgents`, `isOnline` |
| `sdk/index.d.ts` | TypeScript declarations — `AgentResult`, `Agent` interfaces |

---

## Installation

### Option A — Via Claude Hub UI (recommended)

1. Open http://localhost:3847/setup
2. Find your project in the table
3. Click "Install SDK"
4. Claude Hub adds the dependency to `package.json` and runs `npm install`

### Option B — Manual

**Step 1.** Add to `package.json` dependencies:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"
  }
}
```

The `file:` path is relative to the project root. All active projects are siblings of `claude-hub/`, so the path is always `file:../claude-hub/sdk`.

If your project is nested deeper:
```
~/Desktop/Boldteq App/MyProject/        → file:../claude-hub/sdk
~/Desktop/Boldteq App/apps/MyProject/   → file:../../claude-hub/sdk
```

**Step 2.** Install:

```bash
cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/MyProject"
npm install
```

**Step 3.** Verify:

```bash
node -e "
const { isOnline, listAgents } = require('@boldteq/agents');
Promise.all([isOnline(), listAgents()]).then(([online, agents]) => {
  console.log('Online:', online);
  console.log('Agents:', agents.length);
});
"
```

Expected:
```
Online: true
Agents: 12
```

---

## Full API Reference

### `callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs?)`

Calls a global agent with a task and waits for the response.

**TypeScript signature:**
```typescript
function callAgent(
  agentName: string,
  prompt: string,
  timeoutMs?: number  // default: 120000 (2 minutes)
): Promise<AgentResult>

interface AgentResult {
  success: boolean   // true if agent ran and returned output
  output: string     // agent's full response (empty string if failed)
  agent: string      // agentName echoed back
  error?: string     // only set if success is false
}
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `agentName` | string | Yes | — | Agent filename without `.md`, e.g. `'koda'`, `'quill'`, `'nova'` |
| `prompt` | string | Yes | — | The task to send. Write it as you would in a Claude Code chat. |
| `timeoutMs` | number | No | `120000` | Max wait time in milliseconds. Increase for complex tasks. |

**Examples:**

```javascript
// Basic call
const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write a tagline for Pinzo')
if (result.success) {
  console.log(result.output)
} else {
  console.error(result.error)
}

// Custom timeout for long task
const result = await callAgent(
  'koda',
  'Build the subscription billing page with plan comparison table',
  300000  // 5 minutes
)

// Fire and forget
callAgent('mira', "Extract lessons from today's Pinzo session")
```

**When `success` is `false`:**

| Error message | Cause | Fix |
|---------------|-------|-----|
| `"Claude Hub not reachable at http://localhost:3847 — is it running?"` | Server is down | `pm2 restart claude-hub` |
| `"Timed out after Xs"` | Task too slow for timeout | Increase `timeoutMs` or break task into smaller prompts |
| `"Claude Hub returned 4xx"` | Bad request or agent not found | Check `agentName` matches a file in `~/.claude/agents/` |

---

### `listAgents()`

Fetches all available global agents.

**TypeScript signature:**
```typescript
function listAgents(): Promise<Agent[]>

interface Agent {
  filename: string     // e.g. 'koda' (no .md)
  name: string         // e.g. 'Koda — Feature Builder'
  description: string  // from frontmatter
  model: string        // 'sonnet', 'opus', or 'haiku'
  body: string         // full system prompt body
}
```

Returns `[]` if Claude Hub is not reachable (does not throw).

**Example:**

```javascript
const agents = await listAgents()
agents.forEach(a => console.log(`${a.filename} (${a.model})`))

// Output:
// arya (opus)
// bolt (sonnet)
// koda (sonnet)
// nova (sonnet)
// ...
```

---

### `isOnline()`

Checks if Claude Hub is reachable. Uses a 3-second timeout.

**TypeScript signature:**
```typescript
function isOnline(): Promise<boolean>
```

Returns `true` if `GET /api/global/agents` responds with 200. Returns `false` otherwise (never throws).

**Example:**

```typescript
import { isOnline, callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'

async function generateCopy(product: string) {
  if (!await isOnline()) {
    throw new Error('Claude Hub offline. Run: pm2 restart claude-hub')
  }
  return await callAgent('quill', `Write a tagline for ${product}`)
}
```

Use `isOnline()` when Claude Hub being down would cause a bad user experience. For background or async tasks, just call the agent and check `result.error`.

---

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `CLAUDE_HUB_URL` | `http://localhost:3847` | Override the Claude Hub endpoint |

```bash

CLAUDE_HUB_URL=http://192.168.1.10:3847
```

The SDK reads this at import time. For the standard single-Mac setup, never set this — the default is always correct.

---

## Usage Examples by Agent

### Quill — Copy generation

```javascript

const listing = await callAgent(
  'quill',
  'Write a Shopify App Store listing for Pinzo. Include: subtitle, 150-word description, 5 key feature bullets. Tone: clear, direct, conversion-focused.',
  180000
)

// Email sequence
const emails = await callAgent(
  'quill',
  'Write a 3-email onboarding sequence for Rankora (AI resume ranker). Day 1: activate. Day 3: engage. Day 7: retain.',
  180000
)
```

### Nova — Research

```javascript
const research = await callAgent(
  'nova',
  'Research the top 5 Shopify ZIP code / delivery area restriction apps. For each: name, pricing, top features, weak points. Then identify USP gaps.',
  180000
)
```

### Vex — Bug diagnosis

```javascript
const diagnosis = await callAgent(
  'vex',
  `Diagnose this error in our Pinzo Shopify app (React Router 7):
  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'shop')
  at authenticate.admin (app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx:15:25)`
)
```

### Koda — Code generation

```javascript
const endpoint = await callAgent(
  'koda',
  `Write a Next.js API route POST /api/rank-resumes:
  - Accepts { jobDescription: string, resumes: string[] }
  - Validates with Zod
  - Returns { rankings: { index: number, score: number, reason: string }[] }
  - Handles errors with proper status codes`,
  240000
)
```

---

## Error Handling Patterns

### Pattern 1 — Simple check

```javascript
const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write tagline')
if (!result.success) {
  console.error('Agent failed:', result.error)
  return null
}
return result.output
```

### Pattern 2 — Distinguish error types

```javascript
const result = await callAgent('koda', 'Build feature', 300000)
if (!result.success) {
  if (result.error?.includes('not reachable')) {
    throw new Error('Claude Hub is offline. Run: pm2 restart claude-hub')
  }
  if (result.error?.includes('Timed out')) {
    // Retry with longer timeout or smaller task
    return await callAgent('koda', 'Build simplified feature', 600000)
  }
  console.error('Agent error:', result.error)
  return null
}
return result.output
```

### Pattern 3 — TypeScript with full typing

```typescript
import { callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
import type { AgentResult } from '@boldteq/agents'

async function generateDescription(productName: string): Promise<string> {
  const result: AgentResult = await callAgent(
    'quill',
    `Write a 2-sentence product description for ${productName}. Benefit-focused.`
  )
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(`Quill failed: ${result.error}`)
  return result.output
}
```

---

## Recreating the SDK from Scratch

If `claude-hub/sdk/` is missing, recreate it:

```bash
mkdir -p "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/sdk"
```

**`sdk/package.json`:**
```json
{
  "name": "@boldteq/agents",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Call any Boldteq Claude agent from any app",
  "main": "index.js",
  "types": "index.d.ts",
  "license": "UNLICENSED",
  "private": true
}
```

**`sdk/index.js`:**
```javascript
const CLAUDE_HUB_URL = process.env.CLAUDE_HUB_URL || 'http://localhost:3847'

async function callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs = 120000) {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs)
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/playground/run`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ agentName, prompt }),
      signal: controller.signal,
    })
    clearTimeout(timeout)
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Claude Hub returned ${response.status}`)
    const text = await response.text()
    const events = text
      .split('\n')
      .filter(line => line.startsWith('data: '))
      .map(line => { try { return JSON.parse(line.slice(6)) } catch { return null } })
      .filter(Boolean)
    const errorEvent = events.find(e => e.type === 'error')
    if (errorEvent) return { success: false, output: '', agent: agentName, error: errorEvent.error }
    const doneEvent = events.find(e => e.type === 'done' || e.type === 'complete')
    return { success: true, output: doneEvent?.output || '', agent: agentName }
  } catch (err) {
    clearTimeout(timeout)
    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
    return {
      success: false, output: '', agent: agentName,
      error: msg.includes('abort')
        ? `Timed out after ${timeoutMs / 1000}s`
        : `Claude Hub not reachable at ${CLAUDE_HUB_URL} — is it running?`,
    }
  }
}

async function listAgents() {
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/global/agents`)
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)
    return await res.json()
  } catch { return [] }
}

async function isOnline() {
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/global/agents`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) })
    return res.ok
  } catch { return false }
}

module.exports = { callAgent, listAgents, isOnline }
```

**`sdk/index.d.ts`:**
```typescript
export interface AgentResult {
  success: boolean
  output: string
  agent: string
  error?: string
}
export interface Agent {
  filename: string
  name: string
  description: string
  model: string
  body: string
}
export function callAgent(agentName: string, prompt: string, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<AgentResult>
export function listAgents(): Promise<Agent[]>
export function isOnline(): Promise<boolean>
```

After creating the files, run `npm install` in each project that uses `file:../claude-hub/sdk`.

---

## Troubleshooting

### "Claude Hub not reachable"

```bash
pm2 status
# claude-hub must show: online

pm2 restart claude-hub
curl -s http://localhost:3847/api/global/agents | head -c 50
```

### SDK not found after npm install

```bash
# Verify the path in package.json is correct
cat package.json | grep boldteq
# Should show: "file:../claude-hub/sdk"

# Verify the SDK source exists
ls "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/sdk/"
# Should show: index.js, index.d.ts, package.json

# Reinstall
npm install
ls node_modules/@boldteq/agents/
```

### Timeout issues

- Default timeout is 120 seconds (2 minutes).
- Complex tasks (Koda building a full feature, Arya planning an architecture) may need 300–600 seconds.
- Pass a higher `timeoutMs` as the third argument: `callAgent('koda', prompt, 300000)`.

### New machine — SDK symlink broken

The `file:` path resolves at install time. On a new machine, just run `npm install` in each project — it re-resolves the symlink to the new absolute path automatically.

```bash

npm install
node -e "const { isOnline } = require('@boldteq/agents'); isOnline().then(r => console.log('online:', r))"
```
